text:
Emma L.: paging: getting alerts for a spike in SSO token validation failures across us-east-1. dashboard shows a burst starting ~1768419950, rate ~3k/min.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED (sev2) — sso-session-flood — Paging on-call (ryan.k)
Ryan K.: on it, looking at auth logs now. can someone drop the exact alert link?
Emma L.: https://grafana/reports/sso-failure-burst — filter = token_validation_failures > 2000/min
Priya S.: I'm seeing odd traffic from a small set of IPs hitting /sso/validate and /token/introspect with malformed assertion payloads. headers look like automated client.
Ryan K.: confirmed. top client_id = app-internal-legacy (shouldn't be active). sending pcap for last 5m to sec slack thread.
Marco A.: trending: error codes are mostly 401 and 400. Some upstream NGINX logs show rapid session creation attempts then immediate validation.
Dave M.: adding context: earlier today we rotated a deprecated SSO signing key for the staging tenant, but not prod. no planned rotate on prod.
Priya S.: got a snippet from logs: `2026-03-14T21:02:14Z WARN validate_token failed client=app-internal-legacy ip=3.85.122.11 reason=signature_mismatch` — but there are also successful validations from same client with different keys.
Emma L.: possible replay or credential leak. initial hypothesis: leaked client secret + script hitting validate endpoint to probe for accepted signing keys.
security-bot: ATTACHMENT — ip-reputation lookup: 3.85.122.11 -> cloud provider large host, lots of malicious reuse. flagged.
Ryan K.: immediate mitigation proposal: 1) block offending IP ranges at WAF 2) disable app-internal-legacy client_id 3) revoke active sessions issued to that client 4) rotate SSO signing key if we detect key compromise. Any objections?
Marco A.: +1. We should also enable stricter rate-limiting on /sso/validate to avoid backend saturation. current rate-limit is generous for internal clients.
Priya S.: I'll run a quick targeted revocation: `POST /admin/revoke_sessions {"client_id":"app-internal-legacy"}` — should remove live tokens. doing it now.
Priya S.: revocation job started, estimated ~45s to propagate across caches.
Emma L.: WAF rule in progress — blocking /token/introspect and /sso/validate from the /22 ranges we saw. patching rule now.
Ryan K.: I've flagged the client in the admin console (disabled). Will follow with audit note.
incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: WAF block applied by Emma L.; client disabled by Ryan K.; session revocation started by Priya S.
Dave M.: customer-impact check: telemetry shows 12 customers with minor 401 spikes but no long-lived outages. UX teams: do we need an outbound notice?
Emma L.: ping product-ops — for now mark as 'investigating'; avoid public notice until we confirm whether key material leaked.
Priya S.: revocation finished. caches cleared. backends show validation failures dropping sharply. attack traffic still hitting but WAF is cutting ~92%.
Marco A.: CPU spiky on auth-prod-1 and auth-prod-2 during the first 6m, now stabilizing. queue depth normalized.
Ryan K.: next steps: security-runbook recommends rotating SSO signing key if we confirm private key exposure. We don't have direct proof yet — need to search logs for token issuance timestamps that correlate to the attacker window. Priya — can you pull issues for tokens issued in last 2 hours for that client_id?
Priya S.: running query: `select * from tokens where client_id='app-internal-legacy' and issued_at > now()-interval '2 hours'` — returning ~42 tokens, 7 of which have last_use>now()-10m. I'll export to secure bucket and share with sec team.
security-bot: SENSITIVE ACTION: export uploaded to s3://redwood-sec-exports/incident-1768420001/tokens.csv (encrypted).
Ryan K.: security team — do we want to rotate signing key now or wait for evidence? If we rotate, coordinate with customers: rotation will invalidate existing sessions for all clients using the signing key unless we publish a grace window.
Dave M.: recommend mitigations tiered: 1) If evidence of private key exfiltration (signed tokens issued by attacker), rotate immediately with phased rollout. 2) If not, keep block + revocation + disable offending client + increased monitoring.
Emma L.: Sec on-call (Marco) — do you want us to start the key rotation dry-run (generate new key, test validate with new key on canary)? avoids full blast.
Marco A.: yes, start a dry-run. Use key_id=k2 and mount to auth-canary. I will run canary validation checks.
Priya S.: dry-run started: created k2 in KMS (rotation candidate). mounted to auth-canary via feature flag. running smoke: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <sample>" https://auth-canary/sso/validate` -> OK.
Ryan K.: good. coordinate with release team if we promote. Also, schedule a 15m handoff to the on-call covering next shift — I'm going offline in ~8m.
Emma L.: @Marco A. can you take over incident lead in the next 10? I'll drop a short summary when I sign off.
Marco A.: taking lead. summary request and stakeout window?
Ryan K.: summary: blocked offending IPs at WAF, disabled compromised client_id (app-internal-legacy), revoked active sessions for that client, implemented rate-limit tightening, created dry-run rotation key k2 on canary. Monitoring remains for token issuance anomalies. Stakeout: 6 hours.
Emma L.: added note: customer impact minor (temporary 401 spikes for ~12 customers during attack window). No data exfiltration confirmed.
Marco A.: acknowledged. on-call handoff: @Marco A. -> incident lead, @Dave M. -> product liaison, @Priya S. -> auth runbook ops, @Ryan K. -> escalation if we need gov/exec comms.
incident-bot: HANDOFF LOGGED: lead=Marco A.; stakeout_until=1768441601; severity=sev2
Priya S.: I'll keep monitoring tokens query and push any suspicious issuance to sec channel.
security-bot: RULE SUGGESTION: add stricter default rate limit for /sso/validate for non-interactive clients and automatic anomaly detection for session churn per client_id.
Dave M.: will open a follow-up ticket for product/ops to notify a small set of affected customers with guidance (re-login recommended) only if we rotate keys.
Marco A.: next immediate action items for the team: 1) continue monitoring 2) complete canary key verification and schedule full rotation if sec confirms compromise 3) write up preliminary incident timeline in #incidents-postmortems. I'll create the doc.
Emma L.: thanks all — logging off now.
Ryan K.: thanks, good job everyone.
Marco A.: standing by — will update every 15m or on new findings.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED — status=mitigated (attack blocked; stakeout active)
